subject: Specifiying priors for the variance/precision parameter for space-time interaction random effects (Kronecker product models)

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: Specifiying priors for the variance/precision parameter for space-time interaction random effects (Kronecker product models)
parts:
Hi INLA Groups,

In space-time Kronecker product models, there are four types of interactions, and the precision matrix for the latent effects often taks the form: \tau Q_T \bigotimes Q_N

In this context, I would like to know, is it possible to assigne a prior for \tau in model II, III and IV? How to translate this into INLA code?

I take the following code as an example:

library("DClusterm")
data(brainNM)
library(INLA)

nm.adj <- poly2nb(brainst@sp)
adj.mat <- as(nb2mat(nm.adj, style = "B"), "Matrix")

brainst @ data$ID3<- as.numeric(brainst @ data$ID)
brainst @ data$ID.Year <- brainst @ data$Year - 1973 + 1

brain.st4.sar1 <- inla(Observed ~ 1 +
                        f(ID3, model = "besag", graph = adj.mat,
                          group = ID.Year, control.group = list(model = "ar1")
                          ),
                      data = brainst@data, E = Expected, verbose = T, family = "poisson",
                      control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))
summary(brain.st4.sar1)

Where should I put the syntex "hyper" for the whole component f(...)?

Thanks in advance.
All the best,
Charles

On Tue, 2021-12-14 at 06:49 -0800, lyh...@gmail.com wrote:
> In space-time Kronecker product models, there are four types of
> interactions, and the precision matrix for the latent effects often
> taks the form: \tau Q_T \bigotimes Q_N
>
> In this context, I would like to know, is it possible to assigne a
> prior for \tau in model II, III and IV? How to translate this into
> INLA code?

you only need to define a precision for one of the terms, as the other
one is scaled automatically (like with scale.model=TRUE argument),

so with this one

f(ID3, model = "besag", graph = adj.mat,
group = ID.Year, control.group = list(model =
"ar1")
),

then the AR1 model has always marginal variance equal to one, so the
precision is the precision in the 'besag' model. You should add argument
scale.model=TRUE which will endure that the besag-model has average
marginal variance equal to 1
